observation.visible_scene: A right hand holds a reflective optical disc (CD/DVD) by its edges against a wooden tabletop; a green 'STAPLES CD-RW' jewel case sits in the lower-left corner. The disc's shiny face shows radial rainbow diffraction bands and a printed inner hub. The hand, disc center, and background stay in essentially fixed image positions throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The radial rainbow color bands (green, blue, orange-red) shift their angular positions around the disc from frame to frame, sweeping around the center rather than translating.

Bright specular reflection spots change on the right half of the disc: absent or faint early, a single bright blob appears mid-sequence near the right edge, and by the later frames two distinct round white highlights are visible on the right side.
The inner hub text ('TDK', 'P24', 'MCD...') keeps roughly the same upright orientation across the whole excerpt, indicating the disc is not spinning about its own center.
The background wood grain and the Staples case do not move, so the camera is stationary; the observed changes are on the disc itself (a change in its tilt/angle to the light), not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the person does before the first frame and after the last frame (e.g., flipping, inserting, or setting down the disc).
The exact hand motion causing the tilt; only the resulting surface-pattern change is visible.
uncertain_details: Whether the disc is purely tilting or also rotating slightly about its center; the hub text suggests little axial spin but the small orientation drift is hard to confirm.
The precise positions/number of the light sources producing the white reflection blobs.
